hook: SCP-5236 is presented as a review packet rather than a finished file: a rejected draft, the Ethics Committee's notes, a second rejected draft, a sealed inquest and finally the approved version. The anomaly itself, a four-dimensional tear in a Site-19 chemistry lab, is almost beside the point. Read it as a detective story about paperwork, with drug use and overwork at the centre.
whyItMatters:
The article is a showcase for the Ethics Committee as an active player instead of a background rubber stamp. Investigator Mallory Gleason, designated E5-2, uses the narrow power to approve containment procedures as a lever against a department head and, eventually, against the O5 Council.

It is also a good example of a file whose format carries the story. The changes between drafts are the clues, and comparing what gets cut, added and redacted is how you solve the case alongside the investigator.
thingsToNotice:
Compare the first two drafts: in the second, Corbett quietly strips out every mention of the narcotics. The inquest then shows Gleason's black moon question at work, a truth-test whose poetic answers mark lies, which Corbett fails and Wnoroski fails out of fear. The drug turns out to be thumper, a home-pressed mix of meth, modafinil and a Class-X mnestic, and Gleason concludes that Elliot's overdose and nightmare tore a hole in spacetime.

The confrontation with O5-10 is the payoff. Lauren admits Corbett has been dealing with Council protection, at O5-3's direction backed by O5-7 and O5-8, then counters Gleason's overreach with a Writ of Recompense, while Gleason uses the earlier review's own demand to prevent recurrence to justify workplace rules. The approved draft redacts Elliot's name and adds hour limits, an amnesty policy, free rehab and penalties for bosses who encourage drug use.
